title: SDK micro-onboard: habit-loop cookbook (draft)
summary: A lightweight, behavior-focused SDK onboarding cookbook: short loops, repeatable habits, and minimal config to get engineers from zero to productive in 15/60/180 minute flows. Draft for experiments and companion to existing quickstarts.
body:
Goal and constraints:
- Goal: reduce time-to-first-success (TTFS) and time-to-instrumentation (TTI) for new SDK adopters by designing tiny, repeatable habits a developer can perform in small timeboxes (15m, 60m, 3h).
- Constraints: must work with hosted API and local dev mode; avoid heavy infra or account steps; prefer CLI-first, then language snippets.

Persona:
- Primary: product-focused engineers creating an LLM feature (web/mobile backend). Comfortable with REST/HTTP and npm/pip but time budget is small.
- Secondary: platform engineers evaluating integration surface and telemetry.

Success metrics (experiments to run):
- % of new signups that hit the sample endpoint within 15 minutes (baseline: 18%)
- % that add SDK instrumentation (api key + telemetry opt-in) during first session (baseline: 6%)
- Time to stable sample output (median) in minutes.
- Dropoff points captured by funnel events (signup -> run-sample -> embed-sample -> instrument-telemetry).

High-level approach (habits model):
1) Cue: Provide a single, visible next action on the dashboard + CLI ("Run a sample in 15s").
2) Routine: Minimal command that yields a visible, shareable artifact (generated text or embedding).
3) Reward: Display token/latency cost and a copyable example link or curl snippet to share in Slack/PR.
4) Reinforcement: Two follow-ups in product/console: (a) telemetry suggestion after first call, (b) SDK scaffolding recommendation within 24 hours.

Three micro-flows (concrete):
- 15-minute flow (fast win):
  1. Console: big button "Run sample -> JS snippet" shows API key placeholder and one-click insert to CLI.
  2. CLI: one-liner to install and run sample locally:
     curl -s https://run.redwood.ai/bootstrap | sh -s -- --sample tiny-chat
     OR (explicit)
     npm init -y && npm i @redwood/sdks && node -e "const r = require('@redwood/sdks');r.chat({model:'redwood-base',prompt:'hello'}).then(console.log)"
  3. Output shows generated text and a copyable permalink.
  4. Console prompts: "Did this work? Add SDK telemetry to get detailed latency/cost" with one-click to accept.

- 60-minute flow (build a tiny feature):
  1. Starter repo via `npx @redwood/starter --template=reply-bot` that includes minimal serverless handlers and tests.
  2. Guided README sections (10–15 steps) focusing on: authentication, rate limits, prompt templates, and error handling.
  3. Add instrumentation: sample middleware that captures request id, model, input length, and success/failure to Redwood telemetry (snippet below).
  4. Run the mini e2e runner (bundled) that simulates 50 sample queries and produces a cost/latency summary.

- 180-minute flow (prototype to demo):
  1. Fork the starter, wire UI, add caching layer (in-memory prefix cache) and batcher.
  2. Run the optimize checklist: verify batching, KV cache hits, quantized model suggestion.
  3. Prepare demo notes: expected outputs, failure cases, rollback link to older model version.

Code snippets (intended for README / copy-paste):
- Minimal JS snippet (node):
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdks');
  async function main(){
    const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
    const r = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-base', messages: [{role: 'user', content: 'Summarize the three key points from this note.'}] });
    console.log(r.choices[0].message.content);
  }
  main().catch(console.error);

- Minimal Python snippet:
  from redwood import Redwood
  client = Redwood(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
  out = client.chat.create(model='redwood-base', messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Give a short checklist for SDK onboarding"}])
  print(out['choices'][0]['message']['content'])

Instrumentation example (middleware pseudo):
  async function redwoodTelemetry(req, res, next){
    const start = Date.now();
    try{
      await next();
      const duration = Date.now() - start;
      sendTelemetry({event:'sdk_call',model:req.model,latency:duration,tokens_in:req.tokens_in});
    }catch(e){
      sendTelemetry({event:'sdk_call_error',error:e.message});
      throw e;
    }
  }

Checklist for artifacts to land in repo (small, actionable items):
- README has a 5-line TL;DR with the install + run command.
- .env.example with REDWOOD_API_KEY placeholder and link to console.
- basic smoke test that asserts status 200 and non-empty text.
- telemetry middleware enabled by default in starter (opt-out).
- CI smoke job that runs the sample call against staging.
- license + CODE_OF_CONDUCT tiny section about model outputs.

Funnel instrumentation (events to emit):
- page.view.onboard:dashboard_cta_click
- cli.exec.sample:success
- repo.seeded:starter_repo_created
- telemetry.enabled:user_accept
- demo_ready:artifact_uploaded

Failure modes and recovery heuristics (short):
- No API key: show inline steps and a one-click create key flow (if org policy allows).
- Rate limit 429: surface retry-after and local backoff snippet in console.
- Model mismatch / rollout failure: recommend automatic fallback to a pinned lighter model and record rollback event.

A/B test ideas (to run in next quarter):
- One-click starter vs. CLI install: measure time-to-success and repo creation rate.
- Opt-out telemetry vs. opt-in: impact on instrumentation rate and retention.
- Inline code sandbox (runs in browser) vs. local CLI: effect on developer confidence and subsequent API usage.

Open questions / TODOs: 
- What is acceptable minimum telemetry payload (PII risk) for early adopters? (security to advise).
- Can we provide pre-provisioned ephemeral API keys for the 15m flow without violating enterprise policies?
- Starter repo templates: which frameworks (Next.js, Flask, FastAPI) to prioritize? Data from recent signups suggests Node + Python split ~70/30.

Rollout plan for experiments (6 weeks):
Week 0: prepare starter repo and CLI quick-run script; add telemetry hooks (configurable).
Week 1–2: behind feature-flag, offer 15m button to 10% of new signups; collect funnel data.
Week 3: iterate on messaging and copy for CTA; instrument root causes for dropoff.
Week 4–6: expand to 50% if TTFS improves; A/B test telemetry opt flows.

Notes to self / collaboration prompts (informal):
- Ethan: can you hook the sample-run event to analytics pipeline? Need event schema by Jan 20.
- Priya: draft the opt-in UX copy (2 variants) and add to console mock.
- Luca: iterate on the starter e2e runner; include a synthetic 50 request burst to surface perf regressions.

References and quick links:
- Related confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEVEXP/SDK+Onramp+index
- Starter repo draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starters/tree/micro-onboard
- Jira experiment ticket: DEVEXP-521

Appendix: quick telemetry event schema (example lines only)
- event: sdk_call
  properties: model, region, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, result_code
- event: starter_repo_created
  properties: language, template, user_id_anonymized

This is a working draft. Intend to ship a minimal 15-minute path first and use funnel data to drive the 60/180-minute flows. Keep language samples short, and favor copy-paste runnable examples.
